title: Nice to Meet You! Where Are You From?
culturalNote: At any Nairobi party or office, the first three questions are always the same: your name, where you're from, and what you do. Kenyans are curious about wazungu and other foreigners — why you came, how long you're staying, whether you like the food — and they're delighted by any attempt at Swahili. "Tuko pamoja" (we're together) is a warm Kenyan way of saying "I'm with you" — and also a casual goodbye.
startingPoint: Saturday evening at a friend's house party in Kileleshwa. A woman with a plate of samosas comes over to say hi.
